recipeName: Chana Dal Fry with Buttered Roti
instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 cup chana dal (split chickpeas), 4 cups water (for boiling), 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil, 1 chopped onion, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tomato (chopped), 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 2 cups whole wheat flour, ¾ cup water (for dough), and 2 tbsp butter.
Step 2: Rinse Dal: Rinse 1 cup chana dal under cold water until the water runs clear.
Step 3: Boil Dal: In a pot, boil 4 cups water, add the chana dal and 1 tsp salt, cook for 30-40 minutes until soft but not mushy, then drain and set aside.
Step 4: Heat Oil: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes.
Step 5: Fry Base: Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds, then add 1 chopped onion and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, sautéing for 5-7 minutes until golden.
Step 6: Cook Tomato and Spices: Stir in 1 chopped tomato, 1 tsp red chili powder, and 1 tsp garam masala, cooking for 5 minutes until the tomato softens and blends with the spices.
Step 7: Fry Dal: Add the boiled chana dal to the pan, stir well, and fry for 5-10 minutes until the flavors meld and the dal is lightly roasted.

Step 8: Prepare Roti and Serve: Knead 2 cups whole wheat flour with ¾ cup water into a soft dough, rest for 15 minutes, roll into 4-6 circles, cook on a tawa for 1-2 minutes per side, brush with 2 tbsp butter, and serve hot with the chana dal fry.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 400g minced beef, 2 tbsp gram flour (besan), 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil, 1 chopped onion, 1 tbsp garlic (minced), 2 tomatoes (pureed), 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 cups water, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup milk, 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp butter.
Step 2: Prepare Kofta Mixture: In a bowl, mix 400g minced beef with 2 tbsp gram flour, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, and 1 tsp salt until well combined.
Step 3: Shape Koftas: Divide the mixture into 10-12 balls, shaping each into a smooth, round kofta, and set aside.
Step 4: Heat Oil: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes.
Step 5: Cook Curry Base: Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds, then add 1 chopped onion and 1 tbsp minced garlic, sautéing for 5-7 minutes until golden.

Step 6: Simmer Curry: Stir in 2 pureed tomatoes, 1 tsp red chili powder, and 1 tsp garam masala, cook for 5 minutes, then add 2 cups water and bring to a boil; gently add the koftas, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the koftas are cooked and the curry thickens.

Step 7: Prepare Sheermal Dough: In a bowl, mix 2 cups all-purpose flour with 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup milk, 1 tbsp sugar, and a pinch of salt, knead into a soft dough, rest for 1 hour, roll into 4-6 circles, and cook on a tawa or oven (200°C) for 2-3 minutes per side, brushing with 2 tbsp butter.
Step 8: Serve Hot: Ladle the kofta curry into a bowl and serve hot with the buttered sheermal.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 small cauliflower (grated), 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander (chopped), 2 cups whole wheat flour, ¾ cup water (for dough), 2 tbsp ghee (for frying), 1 tbsp butter, and 1 cup yogurt.
Step 2: Prepare Cauliflower: Grate 1 small cauliflower (about 2 cups), squeeze out excess water using a cloth, and place in a bowl.
Step 3: Mix Filling: Add 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp chopped coriander to the grated cauliflower, mixing well.
Step 4: Knead Dough: In a separate bowl, mix 2 cups whole wheat flour with ¾ cup water, knead for 5-7 minutes into a soft dough, and rest for 15 minutes.
Step 5: Divide Dough: Divide the rested dough into 4-6 equal balls.
Step 6: Stuff Paratha: Roll each ball into a 3-inch circle, place 1-2 tbsp of the cauliflower mixture in the center, pinch the edges to seal, and flatten gently.
Step 7: Roll and Fry: Roll each stuffed ball into a 6-7 inch circle, heat a tawa over medium heat, and fry each paratha with ½ tbsp ghee per side for 1-2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Step 8: Serve with Toppings: Plate the hot gobi paratha, top with 1 tbsp butter, and serve with 1 cup yogurt on the side.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 500g beef (shank or stew cuts), ½ cup wheat grains, ¼ cup barley, ¼ cup chana dal, ¼ cup moong dal, 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 6 cups water, 2 tbsp ghee, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup water, 1 tsp garlic (minced), and 1 tbsp ghee (for naan).
Step 2: Soak Grains and Lentils: Rinse ½ cup wheat grains, ¼ cup barley, ¼ cup chana dal, and ¼ cup moong dal, then soak in water for 4-6 hours.
Step 3: Cook Beef: In a pot, add 500g beef, 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, and 6 cups water, boil, then simmer for 1.5-2 hours until tender.
Step 4: Cook Grains and Lentils: In a separate pot, boil the soaked grains and lentils in 4 cups water for 30-40 minutes until soft, then drain.
Step 5: Shred Beef: Remove the beef from the broth, shred it with a fork, and reserve the broth.

Step 6: Blend Haleem: Combine the shredded beef, cooked grains, and lentils in a pot, add some reserved broth, and blend with a hand blender or mash until smooth; slow-cook with 2 tbsp ghee for 20-30 minutes until thick and creamy.

Step 7: Prepare Garlic Naan Dough: In a bowl, mix 2 cups all-purpose flour with 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup water, and a pinch of salt, knead into a soft dough, rest for 1 hour, roll into 4-6 ovals, and spread 1 tsp minced garlic on top.
Step 8: Cook Naan and Serve: Heat a tawa or oven (250°C), cook each naan for 2-3 minutes per side until puffed and golden, brush with 1 tbsp ghee, and serve hot with the beef haleem.

recipeName: Achari Chicken Handi with Tandoori Roti
instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 200g chicken (boneless or bone-in, cubed), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp achari masala, ½ cup yogurt, 1 tsp salt, 1 tomato (chopped), 2 cups whole wheat flour, 1 cup water (for dough), and 1 tbsp ghee.
Step 2: Heat Oil: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a handi or deep pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes.
Step 3: Fry Aromatics: Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Step 4: Cook Chicken: Add 200g chicken pieces, stirring for 5-7 minutes until the chicken changes color and starts to brown.
Step 5: Add Achari Base: Stir in 2 tbsp achari masala, ½ cup yogurt, 1 tsp salt, and 1 chopped tomato, mixing well to coat the chicken.
Step 6: Simmer Handi: Cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the oil separates from the gravy.

Step 7: Prepare Tandoori Roti Dough: In a bowl, knead 2 cups whole wheat flour with 1 cup water into a soft dough, rest for 15 minutes, roll into 4-6 circles, and cook on a tawa or oven (250°C) for 2-3 minutes per side until charred, brushing with 1 tbsp ghee.
Step 8: Serve Hot: Plate the achari chicken handi and serve hot with the tandoori roti.

recipeName: Fish Masala Curry with Buttered Naan
instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 150g fish fillets (e.g., cod or tilapia), 2 tbsp oil, 1 onion (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 1 tomato (chopped), 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup water, and 2 tbsp butter.
Step 2: Prepare Fish: Rinse 150g fish fillets, pat dry, cut into bite-sized pieces, and set aside.
Step 3: Sauté Base: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat, add 1 chopped onion and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, sautéing for 5-7 minutes until golden.
Step 4: Cook Masala: Add 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, and 1 chopped tomato, cooking for 5 minutes until the tomato softens into a thick masala.
Step 5: Simmer Fish: Add the fish pieces and ½ cup water, cover, and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the fish is tender and the curry thickens.

Step 6: Make Buttered Naan: Mix 2 cups all-purpose flour with 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup water, and a pinch of salt, knead into a soft dough, rest for 1 hour, roll into 4-6 ovals, cook on a tawa for 2-3 minutes per side, and brush with 2 tbsp butter.
Step 7: Serve Hot: Ladle the fish masala curry into bowls and serve with warm buttered naan.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 200g mutton (preferably shank), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 onion (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp black cumin (kala jeera), 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp wheat flour, 4 cups water, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup milk, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame seeds, and 1 tbsp ghee.

Step 4: Cook Mutton: Add 200g mutton, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp black cumin, and 1 tsp salt; cook for 10-15 minutes until the meat browns.

Step 7: Prepare Roghni Naan: Mix 2 cups all-purpose flour with 1 tsp yeast, ½ cup milk, 1 tbsp sugar, and a pinch of salt, knead into a soft dough, rest for 1 hour, roll into 4-6 ovals, sprinkle with 1 tsp sesame seeds, cook on a tawa for 2-3 minutes per side, and brush with 1 tbsp ghee.
Step 8: Serve Hot: Ladle the mutton kunna into bowls and serve hot with warm roghni naan.

recipeName: Beef Haleem with Fried Onions & Lemon
instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 400g beef (stew cuts), ½ cup wheat grains, ¼ cup barley, ¼ cup chana dal, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 4 cups water, 1 onion (sliced), oil (for frying), 1 lemon, and 2 tbsp coriander (chopped).
Step 2: Soak Grains: Rinse ½ cup wheat grains, ¼ cup barley, and ¼ cup chana dal; soak in water for 4-6 hours, then drain.
Step 3: Cook Beef and Grains: In a pot, combine 400g beef, soaked grains, and 4 cups water; boil, then simmer for 2-3 hours until the beef is tender and grains are soft.
Step 4: Shred Beef: Remove beef, shred it finely, and return it to the pot with the grains.
Step 5: Blend Haleem: Use a hand blender or masher to blend the mixture into a thick, creamy paste, adding water if needed for consistency.
Step 6: Season Haleem: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pan, add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp garam masala, and 1 tsp salt; stir into the haleem and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Step 7: Fry Onions: Heat oil in a pan, fry 1 sliced onion until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Step 8: Serve Hot: Ladle the haleem into bowls, top with fried onions, 2 tbsp chopped coriander, and lemon wedges, and serve hot..

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 cup mango pulp (fresh or canned), 1 cup full-cream yogurt, 2 tbsp sugar, ¼ tsp cardamom powder, 2 tbsp milk, and a few ice cubes.

Step 5: Adjust Texture: Add a few ice cubes for a frosty texture, blending briefly to incorporate without diluting the flavor too much.
Step 6: Serve Chilled: Pour the mango lassi into chilled glasses, garnish with a pinch of cardamom if desired, and serve immediately.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 cup almonds, ½ cup milk, ¾ cup sugar, ¼ cup ghee, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp slivered almonds (for garnish), and a pinch of saffron (optional).
Step 2: Soak Almonds: Soak 1 cup almonds in warm water for 4-6 hours or overnight to soften, then drain.
Step 3: Peel Almonds: Peel the soaked almonds by gently squeezing them to remove the skins, then pat dry.
Step 4: Grind Almonds: Blend the peeled almonds with ½ cup milk to form a smooth paste, adding a little more milk if needed to blend easily.
Step 5: Cook Paste: Heat ¼ cup ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat, add the almond paste, and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it releases a nutty aroma.

Step 6: Add Sugar and Flavor: Stir in ¾ cup sugar, ½ tsp cardamom powder, and a pinch of saffron (if using); cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring until the mixture thickens into a halwa consistency and starts leaving the pan’s sides.
Step 7: Garnish and Serve: Remove from heat, transfer to a serving dish, garnish with 1 tbsp slivered almonds, and serve warm.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 cup full-fat yogurt, ½ cup water, 2 tbsp sugar, ¼ cup heavy cream, a pinch of cardamom powder (optional), and a few ice cubes.
Step 2: Chill Yogurt: Place 1 cup full-fat yogurt in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes to ensure it’s cold before blending.
Step 3: Blend Base: In a blender, combine the chilled yogurt, ½ cup water, and 2 tbsp sugar; blend for 20-30 seconds until smooth.
Step 4: Add Cream: Pour in ¼ cup heavy cream and a pinch of cardamom powder (if using), blending for another 20-30 seconds until frothy and well-mixed.
Step 5: Adjust Texture: Add a few ice cubes and blend briefly for a chilled, airy consistency, ensuring the lassi remains thick and creamy.
Step 6: Serve Chilled: Pour the lassi into chilled glasses, garnish with a drizzle of cream if desired, and serve immediately.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 2 cups whole wheat flour, ¾ cup water, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp ghee, ¼ cup desi makhan (full-fat homemade butter), and 1 tbsp honey.
Step 2: Prepare Paratha Dough: Mix 2 cups whole wheat flour with 1 tsp salt and ¾ cup water, knead into a soft dough, and rest for 15 minutes.
Step 3: Roll Paratha: Divide dough into 4-6 balls, roll each into a 7-8 inch circle, and lightly brush with ½ tsp ghee.
Step 4: Cook Paratha: Heat a tawa over medium heat, cook each paratha for 1-2 minutes per side, adding ½ tbsp ghee per side, until golden and slightly crisp.
Step 5: Apply Makhan: While the paratha is still warm, spread 1 tbsp desi makhan generously over the top of each paratha.
Step 6: Serve Warm: Drizzle 1 tbsp honey over the makhan-topped paratha and serve immediately for a warm, indulgent treat.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 2 ripe bananas, 4 pitted dates, 1 cup full-fat milk, ½ cup plain yogurt, ½ tsp cardamom powder (optional), and a few ice cubes.

Step 3: Peel Bananas: Peel 2 ripe bananas, break them into smaller chunks, and set aside for blending.

Step 5: Adjust Texture: Add a few ice cubes and blend briefly for a chilled, frothy consistency, or adjust with a splash of milk if a thinner smoothie is desired.
Step 6: Serve Immediately: Pour the creamy banana and date smoothie into glasses and serve right away to enjoy its fresh, rich flavor.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 liter full-fat milk, ½ cup condensed milk, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 8-10 rasgullas (store-bought or homemade), 2 tbsp pistachios (chopped), 1 tsp rose water (optional), and a pinch of saffron (optional).
Step 2: Boil Milk: Pour 1 liter full-fat milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed pan and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Step 3: Add Condensed Milk: Stir in ½ cup condensed milk, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently, until the milk thickens slightly.
Step 4: Flavor Milk: Add ½ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tsp rose water (if using), and a pinch of saffron (if using), stirring for 2-3 minutes to infuse the flavors.
Step 5: Add Rasgullas: Gently squeeze 8-10 rasgullas to remove excess syrup, add them to the milk mixture, and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing them to soak up the creamy milk.
Step 6: Cool Mixture: Remove from heat, let the ras malai cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for 2-3 hours to chill thoroughly.
Step 7: Garnish and Serve: Spoon the chilled ras malai into bowls, ensuring each serving has rasgullas and milk, garnish with 2 tbsp chopped pistachios, and serve cold.

recipeName: Nutty Caramel Fudge with Desi Ghee
instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 1 cup sugar, ½ cup heavy cream, ¼ cup desi ghee, ¼ cup mixed nuts (almonds, cashews, chopped), ½ tsp vanilla essence, a pinch of salt, and 1 tbsp milk (optional, for smoothness).
Step 2: Prepare Tray: Grease a small square tray or plate with 1 tsp desi ghee and line with parchment paper for easy removal.
Step 3: Make Caramel: Heat 1 cup sugar in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat, stirring gently for 5-7 minutes until it melts into a golden caramel.
Step 4: Add Cream and Ghee: Carefully stir in ½ cup heavy cream, ¼ cup desi ghee, and a pinch of salt, mixing slowly for 2-3 minutes until smooth; add 1 tbsp milk if the mixture is too thick.
Step 5: Add Nuts and Flavor: Remove from heat, stir in ¼ cup chopped mixed nuts and ½ tsp vanilla essence, mixing well to distribute evenly.
Step 6: Set Fudge: Pour the caramel mixture into the prepared tray, spreading it evenly with a spatula to about ½-inch thickness, and let it cool at room temperature for 1-2 hours.
Step 7: Slice and Serve: Once set, cut the fudge into squares or rectangles using a sharp knife and serve at room temperature or chilled.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect ½ cup all-purpose flour, ¼ cup semolina (sooji), 1 cup milk, 1 tsp fennel seeds, ¼ tsp cardamom powder, ½ cup ghee (for frying), and ¼ cup honey.

Step 2: Prepare Batter: In a bowl, mix ½ cup all-purpose flour, ¼ cup semolina, 1 tsp fennel seeds, and ¼ tsp cardamom powder; gradually add 1 cup milk, whisking to form a smooth, thick batter, and rest for 15 minutes.
Step 3: Heat Ghee: Heat ½ cup ghee in a shallow frying pan over medium heat until hot but not smoking.
Step 4: Fry Malpua: Pour a small ladleful (about 2 tbsp) of batter into the hot ghee to form a 3-4 inch pancake; fry for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Step 5: Repeat Frying: Repeat the frying process with the remaining batter, adding more ghee if needed, to make 6-8 malpuas, keeping them warm.
Step 6: Drizzle Honey: Arrange the warm malpuas on a serving plate and drizzle ¼ cup honey evenly over them, ensuring each pancake is lightly coated.
Step 7: Serve Warm: Serve the honey-drizzled malpuas immediately while warm, optionally garnished with a sprinkle of crushed pistachios for extra flair.

instructions: Step 1: Gather Ingredients: Collect 2 cups desiccated coconut, ¾ cup condensed milk, ½ tsp cardamom powder, ¼ cup ghee, 2 tbsp milk (optional, for binding), and 2 tbsp coconut powder (for coating).
Step 2: Mix Coconut Base: In a large bowl, combine 2 cups desiccated coconut, ¾ cup condensed milk, and ½ tsp cardamom powder, stirring well to form a sticky mixture; add 2 tbsp milk if too dry.
Step 3: Cook Mixture: Heat a non-stick pan over low heat, add the coconut mixture, and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly until it thickens slightly and comes together.
Step 4: Cool Slightly: Remove from heat and let the mixture cool for 5-10 minutes until it’s comfortable to handle but still warm.
Step 5: Shape Ladoos: Grease your hands with a little ghee, take small portions of the mixture, and roll into 10-12 smooth, round balls (ladoos).
Step 6: Coat with Ghee: Warm ¼ cup ghee slightly, dip or brush each ladoo lightly in the ghee to coat, then roll in 2 tbsp coconut powder for a final touch.
Step 7: Set and Serve: Place the ladoos on a plate, let them set at room temperature for 30 minutes, and serve or store in an airtight container.
